item.title: Drone Hits Tank at Libyan Refinery, Threatening Oil Facilities
item.author: Sherif Tarek and Hatem Mohareb
item.content:encoded: A drone attack on an oil refinery in western Libya destroyed a storage tank, putting oil facilities at risk and potentially aggravating fuel shortages in the OPEC nation.

item.title: NZ National Party to Meet as Leadership Pressure Mounts on Luxon
item.author: Ainsley Thomson
item.content:encoded: New Zealand’s governing National Party will hold a meeting tonight as speculation mounts that its lawmakers are trying to remove Prime Minister Christopher Luxon as leader less than three months before a general election.

item.title: Brouillette: Strait Control Is Iran's "Nuclear Weapon"
item.content:encoded: Former US Energy Secretary Dan Brouillette says Iran's ability to control traffic through the Strait of Hormuz gives Tehran powerful leverage, arguing that control of the waterway is "in fact, a nuclear weapon." Brouillette says ships are not moving through the Strait at normal levels despite President Donald Trump's assertion that it is open, and warns prolonged disruption could establish a higher floor for oil prices because of the added risk premium. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Congress Has Power to Set AI Guardrails: Vogel
item.content:encoded: Miriam Vogel, president and CEO of EqualAI and co-author of Governing the Machine, says Congress has the power to establish guardrails and accountability frameworks for companies using artificial intelligence as increasingly autonomous systems raise questions about human oversight. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Conley: Trump 'Does Not Have Many Options' on Iran
item.content:encoded: Heather Conley, Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute and Former Deputy Assistant Secretary of State, says dwindling targets and munitions are limiting President Donald Trump's options on Iran as hardliners in Tehran toughen their position. Conley says "nothing has shifted on the ground" in the Strait of Hormuz, with little traffic getting through, and argues Iran continues to view the waterway as a key source of leverage. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Markets Open the Week Flat as Oil Prices Rise | The Close 8/10/2026
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Rithholtz Wealth Management Chief Market Strategist Callie Cox, Needham Senior Analyst Ryan MacDonald, Former Kansas City Fed President & CEO Thomas Hoenig, Kayne Anderson Rudnick Portfolio Manager, Senior Research Analyst Julie Biel, Founder ETFs Partner and Portfolio Manager Michael Monaghan, Evercore ISI International Political Affairs & Public Policy Chief Strategist Sarah Bianchi, Gotham Greens CEO Craig Stevenson, & Former NFL Linebacker Bart Scott. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wisconsin’s Roller Coaster of a Democratic Primary Race for Governor Crashes to an End
item.author: Jess Bidgood
item.content:encoded: Democrats appear likely to nominate a democratic socialist for governor. How did they get here?

item.title: Burnham Touts Plans to Crack Down on UK Vaping, Betting Shops
item.author: Joe Mayes
item.content:encoded: Andy Burnham is detailing plans to crack down on the number of new vaping and betting shops, his latest announcement focused on tackling everyday issues as he tries to win over voters since becoming Britain’s prime minister.

item.title: Sanders Calls on A.I. Companies to Pause Development to ‘Avoid Disaster’
item.author: Lisa Lerer
item.content:encoded: Senator Bernie Sanders warned that corporations have already lost control of technology that could cause “potentially cataclysmic results” for millions of people.

item.title: D.C.-Area Airport to Close for 3 Hours for Grand Prix Event
item.author: Karoun Demirjian
item.content:encoded: The Federal Aviation Administration has imposed other closures at Reagan National Airport over events for the 250th anniversary of the nation’s founding.

item.title: Jones Act Relief Extended, Iran War Presses On | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 8/10/2026
item.content:encoded: President Trump extended a waiver Monday for foreign ships transporting oil around the US as the war in Iran continues to disrupt supply chains. Bloomberg News' Mike McKee & Bloomberg Economics' Chris Kennedy explain the implications. Then, Grindr CEO George Arison discusses how the app is transforming to an AI-native platform. Plus, US Antimony Chairman & CEO Gery Evans discusses his company's work with the Trump Administration as it works to boost the US weapons stockpile and supply of critical minerals. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Michigan Senate Race Sets Stage for Midterms and 2028
item.author: Nancy Cook
item.content:encoded: Will progressives become power brokers in the next presidential election?

item.title: Turkey Passes Law to Achieve Peace With Kurdish Separatists
item.author: Murat Oztaskin and Selcan Hacaoglu
item.content:encoded: Turkish lawmakers adopted legislation laying out the dissolution of a Kurdish separatist group and paving the way for one of the world’s longest insurgencies to come to an end.

item.title: Trump Wants to Split Up the MMR Vaccine
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump signed an executive order to recommend breaking up the combined measles, mumps and rubella vaccine into three separate shots and overhauling the national childhood vaccination recommendations. He speaks in the Oval Office. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Downplays Talks With Warsh Amid Fed Independence Doubts
item.author: Josh Wingrove and Courtney Subramanian
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump played down the frequency and length of his conversations with Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh, which raised fresh questions about whether he was seeking to directly influence the central bank.

item.title: Trump Signals Restraint on Iran | Balance of Power 8/10/2026
item.content:encoded: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Joe Mathieu discusses the latest from the Middle East. On today's show, Democratic Congresswoman Suzan DelBene of Washington, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Princeton University Professor Bernard Haykel. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ben Jones, ‘Dukes of Hazzard’ Actor and Congressman, Dies at 84
item.author: Glenn Rifkin
item.content:encoded: He played the mechanic Cooter Davenport on the hit television series before serving two terms as a Democratic congressman from Georgia.

item.title: Trump Ready to Let Economic Pressure Build on Iran
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump says he's ready to let economic pressure build on Iran. He also says the country should pay for damages it has caused to neighbors. Bloomberg's Josh Wingrove reports from the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Democrat Candidates Aren't 'Cookie Cutter,' Says DCCC Chair DelBene
item.content:encoded: Representative Suzan DelBene, who heads the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, said Democratic candidates aren't 'cookie-cutter' and that they reflect their communities and the issues that matter to voters in their home districts. DelBene said that the path to winning back the house runs through purple districts around the country and that candidates running in those districts have 'crossover appeal.' (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hegseth Renames Base for Lindsey Graham
item.author: John Ismay
item.content:encoded: Joint Base Charleston will now be known as Joint Base Lindsey Graham. The senator served as a judge advocate general before retiring as a colonel in 2015.

item.title: Can Trump Influence the Federal Reserve and Interest Rates?
item.author: Enda Curran
item.content:encoded: Since the start of his second term, President Donald Trump has waged a fierce campaign to impose his will on the Federal Reserve, breaking with the modern convention of walling off the US central bank from political interference, at least publicly. He sought to pressure Jerome Powell, the Fed chairman Trump appointed during his first presidential term, to cut interest rates. And he has attempted to push another Fed governor, Lisa Cook, from her job.

item.title: Trump Makes Sweeping New Demands on Iran as Deal Hopes Dim
item.author: Josh Wingrove and Patrick Sykes
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump made sweeping new demands on Iran after Tehran reiterated requests for reparations as part of talks to wind down the conflict, dimming hopes of a quick deal that would reopen the vital Strait of Hormuz as oil prices surged once again.

item.title: Russia Bars Anti-War Yabloko Party From Parliamentary Elections
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: Russia’s Supreme Court blocked the Yabloko party from appearing on the ballot in September’s elections to the lower house of parliament, effectively banning one of the country’s few political blocs openly calling for an end to the fighting in Ukraine.

item.title: Trump Extends Narrowed Waiver of US Jones Act Shipping Mandates
item.author: Jennifer A. Dlouhy
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump has extended a waiver allowing foreign ships to transport oil and other commodities around the US for 90 more days, albeit with new limits, as the war in Iran disrupts crude flows and hikes fuel costs.

item.title: Trump Concedes There Was ‘Some Contractor Error’ in Reflecting Pool Renovations
item.author: David A. Fahrenthold
item.content:encoded: The president had insisted for weeks that the landmarks’ algae-stained waters and peeling lining were the fault of vandals, not the project itself.

item.title: Trump Shrugs Off A.I. and Data Center Concerns as Voters Grow Anxious
item.author: Tony Romm
item.content:encoded: The president and his top aides have been especially bullish about data centers, despite national blowback against the facilities.

item.title: Trump Wins Permission to Remove Brand Damage From BBC Suit
item.author: Erik Larson and Zoe Tillman
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump won permission to revise his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the British Broadcasting Corp. by excluding his earlier claim that a 12-second clip in a documentary caused massive financial damage to his business.

item.title: Minnesota’s Democratic Senate Primary Pits Angie Craig Against Peggy Flanagan
item.author: Ernesto Londoño and Tim Balk
item.content:encoded: The Senate primary race in Minnesota will be the latest test of left-wing energy in the party, in a state that was convulsed by the Trump administration’s deadly immigration crackdown this winter.

item.title: The Campaign Tactics Helping Progressives Win Primaries Ahead of the 2026 Midterms
item.author: Kellen Browning, Tim Balk and Dan Simmons
item.content:encoded: Progressives are being outspent and are receiving little support from the Democratic Party. Their tactics show a different way to succeed.

item.title: Obama and Abdul El-Sayed Discuss Unity After Michigan Senate Primary
item.author: Tim Balk and Bayliss Wagner
item.content:encoded: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed’s call with the former president comes as he tries to win over wary Democrats in Michigan’s high-stakes Senate race.

item.title: Trump Names Will Scharf as White House Counsel
item.author: Maggie Haberman
item.content:encoded: The president said Mr. Scharf, a deeply conservative lawyer and the current staff secretary, would replace David Warrington in early September.

item.title: Michigan Senate Candidate, a Former Trump Critic, Shifts Toward Election Skepticism
item.author: Beth Reinhard
item.content:encoded: Mike Rogers, the Republican nominee, has suggested that further scrutiny of the 2020 election was warranted and that voting irregularities sank his first Senate bid two years ago.

item.title: A Democratic Socialist Seeks New Voters in an Unlikely Place: Fox News
item.author: Jeremy W. Peters
item.content:encoded: Gustavo Gordillo, a leader of the New York D.S.A., wants to reach new voters. But in interviews with conservative media, the backlash can be sharp.

item.title: Trump Crypto Took $100 Million From a Businessman With Red Flags
item.author: Russ Buettner
item.content:encoded: The curious case of Guren “Bobby” Zhou shows the ease with which investors with shady backgrounds and unknown motivations can funnel money to the president.

item.title: The Lonely Crew at the Kennedy Center Will Miss Its…Mice
item.author: Elizabeth Williamson
item.content:encoded: Employees say the performing arts center’s quirky-looking mice have an exotic back story. Do they?

item.title: A Democrat Sounds the Alarm on Christian Nationalism in Congress
item.author: Annie Karni
item.content:encoded: Representative Jared Huffman of California, the only self-declared “humanist” in Congress, writes in a new book that the separation of church and state is in grave danger.
